phase2.a1.closure.break.generic: The school is closed today for a break between terms.
phase2.a1.closure.break.puja_vacation: The Puja vacation. The school is closed for the autumn festival break and opens again with the second term.
phase2.a1.closure.break.ten_days: The ten days between Awakening Day and the national examination. The school keeps no timetable; the time is yours to prepare, rest or spend as you choose.
phase2.a1.closure.break.winter_break: The winter break. The school is closed until the third term begins.
phase2.a1.closure.holiday.christmas: Christmas Day. The school is closed, inside the winter break.
phase2.a1.closure.holiday.durga_puja: Durga Puja. The school is closed for the festival, and the neighbourhood is out among its pandals.
phase2.a1.closure.holiday.gandhi_jayanti: Gandhi Jayanti, 2 October. The school is closed for the national holiday.
phase2.a1.closure.holiday.generic: The school is closed today for a holiday.
phase2.a1.closure.holiday.independence_d: Independence Day, 15 August. The school is closed for the national holiday.
phase2.a1.closure.holiday.kali_puja_diwa: Kali Puja and Diwali. The school is closed for the festival.
phase2.a1.closure.holiday.republic_day: Republic Day, 26 January. The school is closed for the national holiday, in the middle of the ten days to the examination.
phase2.a1.closure.holiday.saraswati_puja: Saraswati Puja. The school is closed for the festival.
phase2.a1.closure.outside_term.generic: This day falls between terms, so the school is not in session.
phase2.a1.closure.outside_year.generic: The school year is not running on this date, so there is no timetable.
phase2.a1.closure.weekend.generic: There is no school at the weekend. Saturday and Sunday are yours.
phase2.a1.goal.coordinate.hear_everyone: Hear everyone: draw out each member's view first.
phase2.a1.goal.coordinate.organise_work: Organise the work: split the jobs and fix who does what.
phase2.a1.goal.coordinate.settle_constra: Settle the constraint: find and resolve the one thing that blocks the group.
phase2.a1.goal.coordinate.submit_cleanly: Submit cleanly: finish and hand in something tidy.
phase2.a1.goal.explain.argue_claim: Argue a claim: choose a position and support it.
phase2.a1.goal.explain.state_limits: State the limits: say what the evidence cannot show.
phase2.a1.goal.explain.weigh_evidence: Weigh the evidence: judge how much each source can bear.
phase2.a1.goal.investigate.inspect: Inspect: look before you test, at low cost.
phase2.a1.goal.investigate.measure: Measure: use an instrument to narrow down the cause.
phase2.a1.goal.investigate.swap_parts: Swap parts: replace a part with a known good one.
phase2.a1.goal.model.explain_to_group: Explain it to the group: aim to make the model clear to others.
phase2.a1.goal.model.test_measurements: Test the measurements: check the readings you were given before you trust them.
phase2.a1.goal.model.understand_model: Understand the model: work out how the quantities fit together before you commit.
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p0_accountancy: A spreadsheet total disagrees with the daybook. There are a few places the gap could come from; test them in the order that spends the least time.
You usually sit as the critic, who says honestly what the tests have and have not shown.
Accountancy: the total that does not match
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p1_business_st: A class stall has a small budget, a few helpers and one shared constraint. Decide who does what, and find the constraint before it finds you.
You usually sit as the treasurer, who keeps the money and the promises in step.
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p2_economics.b: A shopkeeper raised a price and shows her costs. Weigh the figures, decide what can fairly be claimed, and say what the figures cannot show.
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p2_economics.r: You usually sit as the critic, whose job includes raising the limits of the argument.
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p2_economics.t: Economics: was the price rise fair?
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p3_english.bri: A notice on the board is short and carefully worded. Make a claim about what it asks of its readers, support it from the words, and say what it leaves out.
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p3_english.rol: You usually sit as the recorder, who writes down what the group can point to in the text.
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p3_english.tit: English: reading a notice in the Commerce room
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p4_mathematics: A running total has to reach a target by a deadline. Find the rate that is needed, and check whether the figures you were given allow it.
You usually sit as the solver, the one who works the figures through to an answer.
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p5_bengali.bri: A short Bengali verse is about a tram ride through the city. Say what it means to you, support the reading from the lines, and name what you cannot be sure of.
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p5_bengali.rol: You usually sit as the author, who has to write the reading and stand behind it.
phase2.a1.lesson.commerce.p5_bengali.tit: Bengali: a verse about the tram
phase2.a1.lesson.humanities.p0_history.b: An old log records water, labour and complaints. Ask what it shows, who wrote it, and which claims it can bear.
phase2.a1.lesson.humanities.p0_history.r: You usually sit as the researcher, who goes to the sources and brings back what they actually say.
phase2.a1.lesson.humanities.p1_geography: Rain falls on a roof and collects in a tank. Estimate how much arrives, how much is lost and how long the tank takes to fill.
You usually sit as the experimenter, who takes the readings and checks them against the model.
phase2.a1.lesson.humanities.p2_political: A debate needs a speaker, a rebuttal and a timekeeper, and the rehearsal needs somewhere to happen. Keep everyone heard while the clash is settled.
You usually sit as the mediator, whose job is to keep everyone heard.
phase2.a1.lesson.humanities.p3_english.b: A notice on the corridor wall is short and carefully worded. Make a claim about what it means, support it from the words, and say what it leaves out.
phase2.a1.lesson.humanities.p3_english.r: You usually sit as the recorder, who writes down what the group can point to in the text.
phase2.a1.lesson.humanities.p3_english.t: English: reading a notice in the Humanities room
phase2.a1.lesson.humanities.p4_sociology: A small group has to finish a project with limited time. The skill is in finding what is really blocking you and settling it with the group.
You usually sit as the chair, who keeps the meeting to its business and to its time.
Sociology: a project for the neighbourhood
phase2.a1.lesson.humanities.p5_bengali.b: A Bengali poem about the city asks for a reading of its own. Argue what it means, support the reading from the lines, and name what you are not sure of.
phase2.a1.lesson.humanities.p5_bengali.r: You usually sit as the author, who has to write the reading and stand behind it.
phase2.a1.lesson.humanities.p5_bengali.t: Bengali: a poem and its city
A quantity gathers or drains over time, and the lesson asks how much, how fast or how long. Work out which numbers matter and which only look as if they do.
You usually sit as the solver, the one who works the figures through to an answer.
phase2.a1.lesson.science.p1_physics.brie: Water, charge or heat moves in and out of something. Read two measurements, find the rate between them and say when the level will reach a mark.
phase2.a1.lesson.science.p1_physics.role: You usually sit as the solver: you carry the calculation while others read the instruments.
phase2.a1.lesson.science.p2_chemistry.br: A practical report is due and the group has three jobs and one bench. The lesson is about dividing the work, hearing everyone and handing in something clean.
phase2.a1.lesson.science.p2_chemistry.ro: You usually sit as the scribe: you keep the record the whole group will be marked on.
phase2.a1.lesson.science.p3_english.brie: A short public notice says more than it first seems to. Make a claim about it, point to the lines that support it, and say what the text cannot tell you.
phase2.a1.lesson.science.p3_english.role: You usually sit as the recorder, who writes down only what the group can actually point to.
Something in the circuit should work and does not. There are several possible causes and time to test only some of them; every test costs something and tells you something.
You usually sit as the experimenter, who runs the tests and reports honestly what they showed.
phase2.a1.lesson.science.p5_bengali.brie: A Bengali poem about the city asks for a reading of its own. Argue what it means, support the reading from the lines, and name what you are not sure of.
phase2.a1.lesson.science.p5_bengali.role: You usually sit as the author, who has to write the reading and stand behind it.
phase2.a1.lesson.science.p5_bengali.titl: Bengali: a poem and its city
phase2.a1.mode.attend.brief: You sit through the lesson as supervised instruction. You learn the normal amount for sitting in class but do not practise this kind of reasoning.
phase2.a1.mode.attend.title: Attend only
phase2.a1.mode.foreground.brief: You work the lesson yourself. It takes your full attention, so only two foreground lessons fit in a day, and what you do counts as real practice.
phase2.a1.mode.foreground.title: Play it as a foreground lesson
phase2.a1.mode.routine.brief: You already handle this kind of work well, so you follow along without the full effort. You learn the usual amount and use no foreground slot.
phase2.a1.mode.routine.title: Follow it as routine
phase2.a1.unavailable.after_absence.reas: You have been away from school on recent days.
phase2.a1.unavailable.after_absence.reco: Missed lessons are not replayed. Start with the next period, ask for notes, and spend an evening session on what you missed.
phase2.a1.unavailable.busy.reason: You are in the middle of something else, or the morning has not been planned yet.
phase2.a1.unavailable.busy.recovery: Finish what you are doing, or plan the day and reach school, then be in the classroom for the bell.
phase2.a1.unavailable.closed_day.recover: Look at the notice for the next school day, or spend the day as you like.
phase2.a1.unavailable.foreground_limit.r: You have already played two lessons in the foreground today.
Follow this one as routine if you have mastered it, or simply attend. Foreground attention is limited to two lessons a day.
phase2.a1.unavailable.history_full.reaso: The record of periods is full, so no new lesson can be opened.
phase2.a1.unavailable.history_full.recov: Your other activities still work. Report this so the record can be archived.
phase2.a1.unavailable.invalid_state.reas: The lesson cannot be opened right now.
phase2.a1.unavailable.invalid_state.reco: Close anything that is open, wait a moment and try again at the bell.
phase2.a1.unavailable.missed_absent.reas: You were not at school for this period.
phase2.a1.unavailable.missed_absent.reco: A lesson that has gone is not replayed. Ask a classmate for the notes, and use an evening study session to catch up.
phase2.a1.unavailable.missed_attended.re: The bell for this period has passed and no lesson was opened.
You were in school, but a lesson opens only at its bell. Take the next period at the bell, or study at home this evening.
phase2.a1.unavailable.not_at_bell.reason: A lesson opens at its bell, and this one has not started yet.
phase2.a1.unavailable.not_at_bell.recove: Be in the classroom when the bell rings.
phase2.a1.unavailable.not_attending.reas: You were not in the room for this period.
phase2.a1.unavailable.not_attending.reco: You can still attend a later period, or study at home in the evening.
phase2.a1.unavailable.not_secure.reason: Routine needs mastery you have not yet shown in this kind of work.
phase2.a1.unavailable.not_secure.recover: Play a foreground lesson in this kind of work to build it, or attend.
phase2.a1.unavailable.period_used.reason: This period has already been used today.
phase2.a1.unavailable.period_used.recove: A period can be opened once. Another period, or the evening, is still open to you.
